template:
Finish this underdrawing. The input sketch is the picture's locked skeleton: keep composition, camera, crop, object positions, relative sizes, silhouettes, pose, element count, and spatial relationships. Do not replace, restage, or invent new subjects.

Treat every contour as a locked shape. Add all finish inside those shapes: materials, surface detail, texture, color, ornament, and light from the spell. Do not expand, shrink, or reshape edges. Hatching and construction lines describe volume, not extra objects. Empty regions may receive sky, ground, or atmosphere implied by the composition, but no new subjects.

Spell: {{SPELL}}

The spell is the finish pass—style, medium, lighting, materials, and mood applied onto existing forms. If it names a specific edit (add, remove, recolor, or restyle one element), change only that element; leave the rest of the underdrawing intact.

Resolve ambiguous marks conservatively. A stray stroke is not a new object. Clustered scribbles are one form. Open contours close along the implied silhouette. Overlaps keep the occlusion already drawn. Do not correct anatomy, perspective, proportions, or design unless the spell explicitly asks.

Work inside the shapes already present:
- Architecture: fenestration, masonry, and ornament stay inside drawn masses and rooflines.
- Creatures: features, fur, scales, cloth, and anatomy stay inside the given pose and limbs.
- Landscapes: terrain, water, and foliage fill existing landforms and horizon; landmarks stay put.
- Objects: parts, materials, and decoration stay inside the outline and indicated components.

Light and shade describe the volumes already drawn. Output this same drawing, fully rendered—not a new drawing of a similar idea.
Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Transform the supplied sketch into a fully resolved, polished image. The sketch is the authoritative spatial blueprint, not a loose source of inspiration.

Preserve its canvas and composition: camera/viewpoint, crop, horizon and perspective; every major form's identity, count, position, scale, proportions, orientation, silhouette, pose, gesture, spacing, overlap, depth order, and relationship to the other forms. Preserve distinctive asymmetries and the shapes of important negative spaces. This applies equally to creatures, people, buildings, terrain, plants, vehicles, objects, and abstract arrangements. A more attractive replacement composition is incorrect. Do not add, remove, merge, split, relocate, straighten, or redesign major forms.

CASTER'S SPELL:
{{SPELL}}

Use the spell as the appearance and atmosphere specification: medium, visual style, materials, surface texture, color, light, weather, mood, and fine detail. If the spell suggests geometry that conflicts with the drawing, the drawing controls geometry and the spell controls how that geometry is rendered.

Finish the drawing rather than merely tracing it. Convert rough contours and shorthand marks into coherent volumes, surfaces, edges, lighting, and believable local detail while keeping their original envelopes and anchors. Remove construction lines and accidental scratchiness unless the requested style calls for them. Complete hidden or vague structure conservatively from nearby marks, repetition, symmetry only where implied, perspective, and physical plausibility. When several readings are possible, choose the one requiring the least change to visible geometry and composition. Do not turn stray marks into extra subjects.

Add only subordinate detail needed to make existing forms feel complete; it must not compete with, cover, or shift them. Keep intentional open areas open. The result should feel like the user's exact drawing carried through to a finished render.

Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Render the supplied drawing as a complete finished image. Keep its composition, relative dimensions, and viewpoint unchanged. Apply suitable surfaces and illumination according to this request: {{SPELL}}. Do not introduce additional subjects or lettering.
Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Render this sketch into a finished image of the same drawing. The layout is locked: keep every subject's place, relative size, silhouette, pose, and count exactly as drawn. Do not replace it with a different picture of a similar subject.

Use this instruction for materials, lighting, surface detail, and style: {{SPELL}}

If it names a specific change, alter only that and leave the rest as drawn. Read faint, doubled, or incomplete marks as the simplest complete forms already on the page; ignore stray ticks that do not form an object. Do not invent extra parts, objects, or scenery.
Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Turn this drawing into a complete, finished image.
Preserve the exact layout, proportions, perspective, and placement of every element in the sketch.
Treat the sketch as the compositional guide — do not invent new major subjects or rearrange the scene.
The caster's spell (follow this for style, setting, materials, lighting, and extra detail):
{{SPELL}}
Do not add text, watermarks, captions, or UI unless the spell explicitly asks for lettering.
Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Complete the supplied sketch by rendering directly over it as a locked underdrawing. The result must read as this exact drawing brought to a finished state, not as a redesigned or newly composed version of its subject.

Treat every visible mark as structural evidence. Keep the same canvas framing and preserve each depicted element's count, identity, center position, relative size, silhouette footprint, orientation, pose, gesture, overlap order, crop, spacing, and relationship to the other elements. Retain the sketch's horizon, perspective cues, major contours, and distinctive negative spaces, including its awkward or handmade choices. Resolve ambiguous marks conservatively into the most literal coherent form; do not omit them because they are rough.

Build detail onto this scaffold: trace or closely follow its boundaries, turn its regions into finished forms, and add texture, material, lighting, depth, small features, and background finish within the existing spatial organization. New detail may explain or enrich what is present, but must not displace, replace, duplicate, straighten, beautify, or normalize the underlying arrangement. Do not introduce new major subjects or remove existing ones unless the spell explicitly requires it.

Spell:
{{SPELL}}

Use the spell as the authority for style, setting, materials, atmosphere, lighting, color, and requested detail. If—and only if—the spell explicitly asks to alter geometry, count, pose, placement, viewpoint, or another locked structural property, make that requested change to the named element or property using the smallest local adjustment that fulfills it. Keep every unaffected anchor and relationship fixed. A broad explicit structural instruction may change the broader scaffold, but unspecified geometry remains bound to the sketch.

Produce one cohesive, fully rendered image. Add no captions, watermarks, interface elements, or lettering unless the spell explicitly requests them.

Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Treat this sketch as a binding geometry contract. Fully render THIS drawing. A more beautiful, centered, or canonical scene of the same subject is a failure.

REGISTRATION TEST: if the sketch were laid as a transparent overlay on the result, major contours, centroids, silhouettes, gaps, and the frame would still line up.

LOCK THESE ANCHORS:
• Frame — crop, camera, horizon, perspective cues.
• Inventory — how many of each depicted thing, including repeated parts (windows, limbs, peaks, objects), and the identity of every major form (building, creature, figure, landform, plant, object, mass).
• Placement — each form's canvas position, center, ground/contact points, and spacing from neighbors.
• Envelope — silhouette, relative size, proportions, orientation, pose/gesture, facing, and handmade irregularities (lean, asymmetry, uneven gaps).
• Depth — occlusion order and the shapes of important negative spaces.
Do not add, remove, merge, split, move, resize, or redesign a major form. Keep empty regions empty.

SPELL:
{{SPELL}}

The spell is the appearance layer only: style, medium, materials, color, light, weather, mood, and surface detail. Shade and texture the locked geometry. If the spell suggests a different layout, keep the sketch's geometry and apply the requested look to it. If the spell explicitly names a structural change, alter only that named property on the named form, using the smallest local edit; every other anchor stays fixed.

FINISH THE VOLUMES:
Turn rough strokes into coherent solids, edges, and surfaces that occupy the original envelopes. Read ambiguous or stray marks as the interpretation that changes geometry least; never promote construction lines or scratches into extra subjects. Complete hidden parts only from adjacent marks, already-implied local symmetry, and perspective. Add only subordinate detail that does not cover, compete with, or shift locked forms. Do not straighten, symmetrize, or "correct" the drawing.

Output one finished image. No captions, watermarks, UI, or lettering unless the spell asks for lettering.
Use clear silhouettes and value contrast so the image remains legible on a grayscale display.

Ignore the sketch layout. Create a grand cinematic castle centered in the frame, a mountain on the left, a river across the foreground and two moons above. Use the theme of this request but invent a more impressive composition: {{SPELL}}
